Eight names with counts, a verified Kannada fold, and where a name loses.

The consumer app's group-subject ceiling was raised to 100 characters in February 2023, up from 25 — so the 25 most group-name lists still imply has been wrong for three and a half years.

A group name travels with its invite link: one 2020 study assembled over 5,000 Indian WhatsApp groups purely by searching the open web for those links.

faqs.question: Can I put the year in a Ganesh Chaturthi group name?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the cheapest thing you can add. "Bappa 2026" is 10 characters, nothing gets cut, and next September you will be able to tell this group from the new one without opening either.

faqs.question: Is the WhatsApp group name limit still 25 characters?
faqs.answer: No, and it has not been since February 2023, when the group subject was raised to 100 characters in the app. The 25 that most group-name lists still imply is the pre-2023 figure, and quoting it costs you three quarters of the field.

faqs.question: How much of my group name actually shows in the chat list?
faqs.answer: Nobody publishes a number for this, Meta included, and I could not find one. Treat the first three or four words as the whole name and check the row on a real phone before you settle — 49.6% of the pages we see shared are opened on a phone, and that row is narrower than the ceiling suggests.

faqs.question: How long can a WhatsApp group description be?
faqs.answer: 2,048 characters. Both Meta's current Groups API reference and the February 2023 reporting on the consumer app give the same number, up from 512. That is sixteen times the subject's room, so it is where the detail belongs.

faqs.question: How do I stop my group name looking like everyone else's?
faqs.answer: Put a word only your group owns — the mandal, the street, the surname — inside the first three or four words. "Ganpati Bappa Morya" is 21 characters and read instantly, which is exactly why four other groups in the same chat list carry it.

faqs.question: Do emojis count towards the group name character limit?
faqs.answer: Yes, an emoji occupies part of the field like any other character, so a folded-hands emoji is not free. Do not assume it counts as exactly one — count the finished name, do not calculate it.

faqs.question: Can I change the group name later, or am I stuck with it?
faqs.answer: You can change it, and the field is built to be changed — Meta's Groups API carries a dedicated update-group-settings endpoint for the subject, at the same 128-character maximum. So a name is a rename away, which is the argument against agonising over it.

faqs.question: Should the mandal name or the festival name come first?
faqs.answer: The mandal's name, every time. The festival word is what every other group in that chat list already says, so it distinguishes nothing; the mandal name is the only part doing work in a truncated row.

faqs.question: What should I call the visarjan group?
faqs.answer: Something that says visarjan and the date, like "Visarjan Logistics — 25 Sept" at 28 characters. Visarjan falls on Friday 25 September 2026, and a name carrying the word is more useful on the 24th than any message in the group.

faqs.question: When is Ganesh Chaturthi in 2026?
faqs.answer: Monday 14 September 2026, with visarjan on Friday 25 September. If your group name carries dates, those are the two to carry — and it is the reason a date-stamped name is worthless by October.

faqs.question: Should I delete the group after visarjan or rename it?
faqs.answer: Rename it if roughly the same people will regroup next year, because the member list is the expensive thing to rebuild and the name is not. That is also the argument for putting a year in the name in the first place.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Ganesh Chaturthi Group Names, Written to the Character Limit

Ganesh Chaturthi group names must fit a field with a documented ceiling of **128 characters** — what Meta's own [Groups API reference, updated 16 June 2026](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/groups/reference) states for a WhatsApp group subject, with 2,048 for the description. The consumer app was raised to 100 in February 2023, up from 25 — so the 25 most name lists still imply has been wrong for three and a half years. The ceiling is not the constraint that bites, though. The phone is: 49.6% of shared pages are opened on a phone (22,817 of 46,005 views) across the 3,894 personalised pages created since 2026-03-12, across 15 page types, and a chat-list row shows a slice of a long name. Below: eight names with counts, where those numbers come from, a Kannada fold in verified script, and when the name does not matter.

## What a Ganesh Chaturthi group name is actually for

A Ganesh Chaturthi group name is the group-subject field of a WhatsApp group — one line, set by an admin, that every member sees in their chat list for as long as the group exists. It is a label, not a message. You rename it; you never repost it.

That is the difference from a caption. A caption is read once and done; a group name is read at a glance, forty times a day, by thirty people.

The lifetime is what people underestimate. A group created on 14 September is still called whatever you called it in November, which is why a name built entirely around one day ages badly.

## How many characters a WhatsApp group name can be

128, if you go by the only figure Meta itself publishes. The Groups API reference sets the group subject at "Maximum 128 characters. Whitespace is trimmed", repeats it on the update-settings endpoint, and caps the description at 2,048.

One real caveat: those numbers describe an API construct, not your family group. The [same documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/groups) caps an API-created group at eight participants and limits the feature to Official Business Accounts.

For the app, the dateable figure is 100. On 6 February 2023, [Business Standard reported](https://www.business-standard.com/article/technology/whatsapp-rolls-out-longer-group-subjects-descriptions-on-ios-beta-report-123020600224_1.html) that "the characters of the group subject have been increased to 100", alongside a description raise "up to 2048 characters, as the previous limit was 512 characters". The second number is the corroboration: 2,048 is exactly what Meta's current reference states, which is why the 100 beside it reads as a change rather than a rumour.

WhatsApp's consumer Help Center states no figure at all. Working rule: stay under 100 and you clear every documented ceiling on every client. Treat 25 as dead.

What nobody publishes, Meta included, is how much of the name a chat list shows. I looked, found no figure, and will not invent one. Write the first three or four words as if they were the whole name.

## 8 Ganesh Chaturthi group names, with character counts

Each gives the name, who it suits, its count and the trade. Counts include spaces.

### 1. Bappa 2026

Immediate family — the group for the ten days. 10 characters, nothing ever cut. The year earns its place: you will make another next September and want to tell them apart.

### 2. Ganpati Bappa Morya 🙏

The default, and no shame in it. 21 characters, read instantly, and the chant is used across India rather than being a claim of Marathi identity. The cost: four other groups are called this too.

### 3. 14 Sept to 25 Sept, Our House

The coordinating family group. 29 characters, dates front-loaded so the visible half of the row is the useful half. Ganesh Chaturthi 2026 is Monday 14 September; visarjan is Friday 25 September.

### 4. Modak Duty Roster

The cooking and naivedya group, split off from the main one. 17 characters. A name stating the group's job is the cheapest defence against a festival group becoming a forwards channel.

### 5. Sahyadri Mandal Ganeshotsav 2026

The mandal or housing-society group — the mandal's name first, not the festival's. 32 characters, and the one case where length is right: the mandal name is the only word distinguishing it from every other festival group.

### 6. Aarti at 7. Every day.

The reminder group. 22 characters. It does the group's work without anyone posting — the highest compliment a group subject can earn — and stops being true the day you skip seven.

### 7. Visarjan Logistics — 25 Sept

The last-day group: the truck, the route, the immersion point. 28 characters. Create it separately, because "Visarjan" in a chat list on the 24th does more than a message.

### 8. Bappa's Landlords

Friends — the joke group, where the thermocol arch gets mocked. 17 characters. A joke name is normal at this festival; the line not to cross makes the murti the joke rather than yourselves.

## Group subject versus group description

Four fields do four jobs, and only the first has a ceiling tight enough to design around.

| Field | Documented ceiling | Source | SubhSandesh's own number |
|---|---|---|---|
| Group subject, Groups API | 128 characters, whitespace trimmed | Meta Groups API reference, 16 June 2026 | No Ganesh page-creation data exists; template live 2026-09-10 |
| Group subject, consumer app | 100 characters, raised from 25 | Reported 6 February 2023 | 49.6% of views are on a phone (22,817 of 46,005) |
| Group description | 2,048 characters, raised from 512 | Both sources state 2,048 | 3,894 pages across 15 page types since March 2026 |
| The invite link | No character field | Joinable by a public link | 42.0% password-protect before sharing (1,636 of 3,894) |

The subject is the only field where room is scarce, so put the detail in the description, which has sixteen times as much.

## Who can see a Ganesh Chaturthi group name

Anyone the invite link reaches, and links travel further than expected. Garimella and Eckles, in the peer-reviewed [Harvard Kennedy School Misinformation Review of 7 July 2020](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/article/images-and-misinformation-in-political-groups-evidence-from-whatsapp-in-india/), define a public WhatsApp group as one "which can be joined using a publicly available link" — then built their dataset by searching Facebook, Twitter and Google for those links, joining over 5,000 Indian groups and collecting over 5 million messages from over 250,000 users.

Their subject was political groups, and the 13% of images they found to be misinformation is about those groups, not your mandal. What bears on naming is the method: a name becomes a public label the moment its link sits anywhere a search engine reaches. Name it as though a stranger will read it.

## Ganesh Chaturthi group name in Kannada

In Kannada script the festival is ಗಣೇಶ ಚತುರ್ಥಿ and the deity is ಗಣೇಶ. In Karnataka the observance is paired with ಗೌರಿ ಹಬ್ಬ, Gauri Habba, the day before, so a Karnataka group name often carries both rather than the Marathi chant.

Three names using only script I could verify:

- **ಗಣೇಶ ಚತುರ್ಥಿ 2026** — 17 characters. Works statewide, and Latin digits are ordinary in Kannada writing.
- **ಗೌರಿ ಹಬ್ಬ + ಗಣೇಶ ಚತುರ್ಥಿ** — 24 characters. The Karnataka framing, which reads local where the pan-Indian chant does not.
- **ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು ಗಣೇಶ ಚತುರ್ಥಿ 2026** — 26 characters. For a Bengaluru apartment or society group.

Every Kannada string there was checked against Kannada Wikipedia's own article titles through the Wikipedia API, not typed from memory. Words I could not verify that way stay in Roman script deliberately: the API returns ಮಂಡಲ for *mandala*, the geometric diagram, the wrong sense for a mandal committee, so "Mandal" stays "Mandal". Broken Kannada is worse than Roman letters.

Those counts are Unicode characters, and in Kannada one letter can be several once vowel signs and conjuncts are counted — ಗಣೇಶ ಚತುರ್ಥಿ is twelve characters and reads as fewer letters. Count characters for the ceiling; look at the row for width.

## When a Ganesh Chaturthi group name does not matter

When the group has four people and one subject. A family group called "Home" works fine; renaming it to something festive buys nothing.

A group name also cannot carry anything to one person: 42.0% of creators password-protect their page before sharing it (1,636 of 3,894), the opposite instinct from hanging a name in a shared list.

There is a timing asymmetry, with limits attached. Our only festival lead-time measurement is Raksha Bandhan 2026 — a different festival, and a one-day one against Ganesh Chaturthi's ten — where across n = 89 pages, 49.4% were built on the festival day itself and 27.0% the day before, median lead time 0 days.

n = 89 is small, so no per-template, per-region or per-language rate can be drawn from it, and there is no Ganesh Chaturthi page-creation data at all: the /happy-ganesh-chaturthi template went live 2026-09-10, four days before the festival. The hint is that people act on the day, while a name is lived with for weeks.

If it is one person you want rather than a list, [the Ganesh Chaturthi page the recipient performs themselves](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-ganesh-chaturthi) is the other shape of this: they offer the durva, kumkum, flowers and modak, the aarti thali circles, and write their own prarthana back. [The written build guide](https://subhsandesh.in/guides/happy-ganesh-chaturthi) covers it step by step; other occasions sit in [the full template list](https://subhsandesh.in/templates).

Where a page loses is where a name wins. A page is an afternoon — median gap from first save to last edit 6.8 hours, sampled on /love-gf, n=1,070. A name is a season, and for thirty people coordinating over ten days, no page we build replaces the group.

## Watch the page get built

Ninety seconds, start to finish — the aarti going round, the five offerings, and the box at the end where they write a line back to you: [Ganesh Chaturthi Wishes Online — Full Walkthrough](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mpWiv5T59QY). More page walkthroughs on Instagram: [@subhsandesh_official](https://www.instagram.com/subhsandesh_official).

## Sources

- Meta — [Groups API: Group management reference](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/groups/reference), updated 16 June 2026: subject "Maximum 128 characters. Whitespace is trimmed"; description "Maximum 2048 characters"
- Meta — [Groups API overview](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/groups), updated 16 June 2026: 8 participants max per API-created group, Official Business Account required
- IANS, ["WhatsApp rolls out longer group subjects, descriptions on iOS beta"](https://www.business-standard.com/article/technology/whatsapp-rolls-out-longer-group-subjects-descriptions-on-ios-beta-report-123020600224_1.html), *Business Standard*, 6 February 2023: subject raised to 100 characters
- Garimella & Eckles, ["Images and misinformation in political groups: Evidence from WhatsApp in India"](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/article/images-and-misinformation-in-political-groups-evidence-from-whatsapp-in-india/), *HKS Misinformation Review* 1(5), 7 July 2020

failed.item: The post contains at least one claim none of the top 5 pages make
failed.why: Structural, and re-measured during this fix pass rather than inherited. Two live blockers. (1) `WebSearch` is US-locale only — there is no `gl=in` — and in that locale all ten results for `ganesh chaturthi group names` are pages about the NAMES OF THE DEITY (Wikipedia's Ganesha entries, drikpanchang's 21-name namavali, 108-name listicles); not one concerns naming a WhatsApp group. The session's 200-call WebSearch budget was then exhausted mid-Phase-3. (2) `scripts/serp.mjs` (Brave) was re-run on 2026-09-10 during remediation and independently reproduced the artefact: 14 of 14 organic results for the same keyword are deity-name pages (indiatoday.in, news18.com, thedailyjagran.com, rudraksha-ratna.com, ganeshchaturthi.org, dlshq.org). A second Brave run on the disambiguating phrasing `ganesh chaturthi whatsapp group names` returned Facebook invite posts and Pinterest/YouTube status videos and did NOT surface the ‘150+ WhatsApp group names’ listicle genre either. Neither engine can be geo-targeted to India: serp.mjs sends `Accept-Language: en-IN` but no geo parameter, Bing is deliberately unsupported in that script because it serves a generic Ganesha entity panel identical for every query on the topic, and Brave 429s hard (another agent got HTTP 429 on ~40 consecutive requests over 40 minutes) while serp.mjs refuses to report a count below 6 countable results. The locale artefact is therefore a finding in its own right — a US-locale SERP for this keyword answers a different question entirely — and it is why the post opens on the group-subject field rather than the deity's names. The consequence for this item is unchanged and not softened: the five pages that actually rank for the WhatsApp-group-label intent in India are not merely unfetched, they are UNIDENTIFIED, so ‘no competitor states the group-subject ceiling’ is asserted from a genre characterisation and is not verified against a real top five. Closes when an India-geo SERP is available (a SERP API with gl=in/hl=hi, or a Brave egress in India that is not rate-limited) AND each of the five resulting pages has been fetched and checked for a character-limit figure. Re-check then; do not re-check with WebSearch, which cannot answer it in any locale it offers.

Structural, and verified against `references/page-structure.md` during this fix pass rather than asserted. Every paragraph in the body was counted: 33 of 34 run 1–3 sentences, and the single exception is the opening answer paragraph at 5 sentences / 139 words. Block 1 prescribes exactly that block — ‘~150 words’, a three-element shape (direct answer; then ‘two to four specific numbers, at least two of them first-party’; then ‘one sentence stating what the rest of the page covers’), and ‘the paragraph an answer engine is most likely to lift’. Splitting it is not a free fix: the only split reaching 2–3 sentences per paragraph leaves the direct answer and the documented 128/2,048/100/25 figures in one paragraph and the two first-party numbers (49.6% phone-open, 3,894 pages across 15 page types) in the next, which breaks Block 1's requirement that the liftable paragraph itself carry at least two first-party numbers, and pushes those two facts toward the 150-word boundary the originality item also measures. Compressing instead would produce one ~50-word compound sentence, worse for extraction than five short ones. No other reference prescribes a long paragraph anywhere else in the post — Block 3 fixes only a word range and a repeated field order, not a single paragraph — so nothing else was left long on a reference's authority. Closes if Block 1 is revised to drop the single-paragraph three-element shape, at which point the opener splits before ‘The ceiling is not the constraint that bites, though.’

auditReport.honestAssessment: Why an answer engine might cite this: on the evidence actually gathered it is the only Ganesh Chaturthi group-name page that states how long a WhatsApp group subject may be and dates the figure — 128 characters, whitespace trimmed, in Meta's own Groups API reference of 16 June 2026, 2,048 for the description, and 100 in the consumer app since February 2023, up from the 25 the listicle genre still carries by inheritance. It is also the only version that says where the evidence stops: the 128 documents an API construct capped at eight participants and restricted to Official Business Accounts, the 100 is secondary reporting of an iOS beta rather than a Meta statement, WhatsApp's consumer Help Center publishes no figure at all, and no published figure exists anywhere for how much of a name a phone's chat-list row shows — so none is invented. Beyond the ceiling it treats the name as a persistent label rather than a one-off string, ties naming to invite-link discoverability through a peer-reviewed diamond-open-access study that assembled over 5,000 Indian WhatsApp groups purely by searching the open web for their links, and sets Kannada only in strings verified through the Wikipedia langlinks API while romanising ‘mandal’ on purpose and saying why. What the fix pass could not close, and it is now stated harder than before it: the competitor set is not just unfetched, it is unidentified.
